nodes.label: Diffuse painful pustular lesions on face, trunk, hands, feet, ankles, and penis
Patient is a 33-year-old Hispanic bisexual man with HIV diagnosed 8 years prior and not receiving antiretroviral therapy; CD4 count 3 cells/mm³ (0%), viral load 43,751 copies/mL at presentation
Initial presentation included dysuria and penile discharge; two weeks later the patient was hospitalized due to worsening diffuse pustular lesions
DNA PCR with whole genome sequencing detects F13L gene mutations confirming orthopoxvirus (mpox)
HSV, VZV, and fungal tests are negative
Blood or CSF mpox PCR and species-level clade/blood dissemination results were not obtained, lacking direct hematogenous confirmation
Visceral imaging was requested but remains unavailable, so organ dissemination is not directly confirmed
Repeated skin PCR testing for mpox is positive, as noted by the laboratory physician
